stories.title: Government promises no one loses free food grains under a planned rewrite of India's food security law
stories.what_happened: Replying to questions in the Rajya Sabha's Question Hour on Wednesday, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Minister **Pralhad Joshi** assured MPs that the draft **National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026** will not reduce food grain allocations to any state or any individual beneficiary. He said the government has formally invited comments and suggestions on the draft bill from state governments before it is finalized. Joshi reiterated that the bill's purpose is to **standardize and equalize entitlements**, moving away from the current household-based calculation that produces inconsistent per-person amounts depending on family size, and correcting variations built up under the 2013 law. He pointed to the scale of the existing safety net, noting that **81 crore people** currently receive free food grains every month under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), which provides **35 kg of free grain per household per month** and is described by officials as one of the largest food security programs in the world.
key_points: Union minister **Pralhad Joshi** told the Rajya Sabha that **no state or beneficiary** will see reduced food grain quotas under the draft **National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026**
The government has invited **comments from state governments** on the draft bill before finalizing it
The redesign aims to move from a **household-based entitlement** to a more **uniform, per-person system**
Currently, **81 crore people** get free food grains every month under the **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana**, one of the world's largest food-security programs
Each covered household currently gets **35 kg of free food grain per month**

depth.background: India's National Food Security Act, 2013, guarantees subsidized or free food grain to roughly two-thirds of the population, but entitlements are calculated per household rather than per person, so a household of 3 and a household of 8 can get the same fixed quota, creating real inequities on the ground. The government floated a draft amendment bill to fix this by standardizing entitlements more fairly, and has been circulating it for state feedback before formal introduction in Parliament. Opposition parties and some states had raised concerns that any 'reform' could be used to quietly cut coverage, which is the specific worry Joshi was responding to.

stories.title: Bombay High Court orders Meta, Google and X to remove deepfake videos falsely tying Nitin Gadkari to India's ethanol-fuel policy
stories.what_happened: The Bombay High Court, in an order by Justice Abhay Ahuja, directed the takedown of deepfake videos and AI-generated images falsely tying Nitin Gadkari to personal financial gain from the E20 ethanol-blending programme. Gadkari's petition said the fabricated content claimed he and his family profit from the policy through his son Nikhil's ethanol company, **CIAN Agro Industries & Infrastructure**. The court found the material "per se defamatory" and "highly abusive," saying it shouldn't be accessible on public platforms, especially to younger users. Meta and Google told the court they would voluntarily remove the specific content identified in the lawsuit, and the court accepted that while ordering the takedown. Justice Ahuja also granted Gadkari permission to pursue legal action against Meta, Google, X, and unidentified individuals responsible for creating and spreading the material.
key_points: **Justice Abhay Ahuja** ordered takedown of AI-generated deepfakes falsely linking Union minister **Nitin Gadkari** to the government's **E20 ethanol-blending programme**.
The fake content claimed Gadkari's **son's company profits from ethanol blending** — an allegation the court found **'per se defamatory.'**
**Meta and Google told the court** they would voluntarily remove the flagged content; the court accepted that and ordered it done.
Gadkari was also given permission to pursue **legal action against unidentified individuals** who created and spread the videos.
The court said the material was **'highly abusive'** and shouldn't remain accessible, especially to **younger users**.

depth.background: India's government has been rolling out **E20** — petrol blended with 20% ethanol — to cut oil imports and emissions, with Union Minister Nitin Gadkari as its most visible champion. The policy has become politically contentious: critics, including opposition politicians, have raised concerns about its effect on vehicle engines and fuel costs, and Delhi Police separately stopped a protest march against E20 fuel just a day earlier. Deepfake videos and AI-generated images began circulating that falsely claimed Gadkari personally benefits from the policy because his son Nikhil Gadkari runs an ethanol-manufacturing company, CIAN Agro Industries — an allegation Gadkari disputes and took to court over.

stories.title: Aston Martin to lose veteran performance chief Tom McCullough at the end of 2026
stories.what_happened: Multiple outlets, including Formula1.com, reported this week that **Tom McCullough will depart Aston Martin entirely at the end of the 2026 season**, ending a 13-year association with the team that began in 2014. McCullough rose to become the team's performance director by 2018, a post he held until Andy Cowell's 2025 restructuring moved leadership responsibilities to Cowell himself and others, shifting McCullough away from Aston Martin's core F1 operation. For the past 20 months he has overseen the team's broader **Performance Technologies** division, which extends Aston Martin's motorsport engineering into categories beyond F1. That role, and his time at the company, will now end.
key_points: Tom McCullough will leave Aston Martin at the end of the 2026 season after **13 years** with the team.
He first joined in 2014 as chief race engineer when the team was still **Force India**.
McCullough had already stepped back from Aston Martin's F1 side in a **2025 management reshuffle** under team boss Andy Cowell.
He's spent the last 20 months running the team's wider **Performance Technologies** motorsport ventures, a role he'll now leave entirely.

depth.background: Aston Martin's Formula 1 team has gone through several names and owners over the past decade — racing as Jordan, then Force India, then Racing Point, before becoming Aston Martin in 2021 under new owner Lawrence Stroll's investment. Tom McCullough has been a constant through much of that transition, rising from chief race engineer to **performance director**, one of the team's most senior technical roles, which he held until the end of 2024. In early 2025, new team principal **Andy Cowell** restructured senior leadership, and many of McCullough's F1 responsibilities were absorbed by others, moving him into a role focused on the team's non-F1 racing ventures.

stories.title: Pakistan's cricket board threatens ex-players with a two-year ban over an unauthorized Zambia league
stories.what_happened: The PCB said on **August 5** that it had taken 'serious notice' of former Pakistan internationals who competed in the **20th Asian Legends League 2026**, held in Zambia, without securing the required PCB clearance. The board confirmed the tournament is considered '**unsanctioned/disapproved**' by the ICC and was also never approved by the **Zambia Cricket Union** itself. Under the PCB's disciplinary framework, any individual found to have taken part without authorization will be barred for **two years** from receiving a PCB No Objection Certificate for approved overseas leagues, and separately barred for two years from taking up any role with the PCB or the **Pakistan Super League**. The PCB has not yet named the specific players facing sanction.
key_points: The **Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB)** warned former internationals who played in the **20th Asian Legends League** in Zambia without approval
Offenders face a **two-year ban** on getting PCB clearance for any future overseas league
They'd also be barred **two years** from any role with the PCB or the **Pakistan Super League (PSL)**
The **ICC** classifies the Zambia event as an '**unsanctioned/disapproved**' cricket tournament
Even **Zambia's own cricket board** says it never approved the league

depth.background: Cricket boards around the world, including the **PCB**, require current and former players to get a **No Objection Certificate (NOC)** before playing in overseas leagues — a rule meant to protect the sport's integrity, ensure proper anti-corruption oversight, and stop unregulated tournaments from operating in a legal and financial grey zone. Retired players, in particular, are drawn to lucrative 'legends league' exhibition tournaments abroad, but boards increasingly police these because unsanctioned events can lack basic safeguards against match-fixing. The **International Cricket Council (ICC)** maintains its own list of tournaments it will not recognize.

stories.title: Lok Sabha adjourned again as Opposition presses for a debate on police action against protesting students
stories.what_happened: When the Lok Sabha convened Wednesday morning, Opposition members trooped into the well of the House, raising slogans and demanding a discussion on police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak. Speaker Om Birla repeatedly asked members to return to their seats, telling them the sloganeering "lowers the dignity of the House," but the protests continued and he adjourned proceedings until 2 PM. Despite the disruption, the government pushed through the **Bankers' Books Evidence (Amendment) Bill**, which tightens rules on using digitized bank records as evidence, with essentially no debate. This is the latest in a string of adjournments since the session began, with Question Hour going uncompleted on most sitting days. The Opposition is also separately pressing for accountability over the alleged theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram temple.
key_points: The House was adjourned till **2 PM** for one of several times this week during the Monsoon Session
Opposition MPs demanded statements from **PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah** on police action against students
Speaker **Om Birla** appealed for order before adjourning amid sustained sloganeering
The **Bankers' Books Evidence (Amendment) Bill** was passed without real debate amid the disruption

depth.background: India's Parliament holds a Monsoon Session roughly from late July into August each year to pass legislation and question the government on recent events. This year's session, which began **July 20**, has been repeatedly disrupted, with the Opposition — including Congress and regional parties — protesting over the **NEET medical-entrance exam paper leak** and an alleged theft of donations at Ayodhya's Ram temple. The latest flashpoint is anger over police action taken against students protesting the paper leak, which Opposition MPs say deserves a full debate and ministerial accountability. Because of the repeated walkouts, the House has struggled to complete even its daily **Question Hour**, the period when MPs are supposed to grill ministers directly.

stories.title: AP investigation: Trump's immigration crackdown has detained over 50 spouses and parents of active-duty US troops
stories.what_happened: The **Associated Press**, in what it calls its first full accounting of the practice, found that more than **50 parents and spouses of active-duty troops** have been detained by immigration authorities since Trump took office for a second term. Of those, **at least six have been deported** and one left the country voluntarily under pressure, while **eight** family members remain in detention as their cases proceed. AP also found that from January 2025 to January 2026, authorities separately detained **125 military veterans**, placing 34 of them into removal proceedings, and arrested more than 150 immediate family members of service members overall. The processing time for military parole-in-place — the legal pathway meant to protect these families — has **more than doubled to about 12 months**, according to USCIS data cited in the report. The story has drawn a rare mixed reaction from Congress: some Republicans who otherwise back Trump's immigration crackdown have pushed for individual relatives to be released, while Democratic senators, including Mark Kelly, have opened a formal investigation into the detentions.
key_points: **More than 50** parents and spouses of active-duty US service members detained since Trump's second term began
At least **six deported** and one self-deported; **eight** family members remain in federal custody
Wait time for legal status under 'military parole-in-place' has **more than doubled to 12 months**
Separately, **125 military veterans** were also detained since Jan 2025, with **34** put into removal proceedings
Democratic senators including **Mark Kelly** have opened a congressional investigation into the policy

depth.background: For decades, under a bipartisan understanding stretching across Republican and Democratic administrations, the US government generally shielded the parents and spouses of active-duty troops from deportation — the logic being that a service member should not have to worry about a parent or spouse being taken away while they're deployed. The main tool for this is **'military parole-in-place'**, a program that lets these relatives apply for legal status without leaving the country. Since returning to office, the Trump administration has pursued an aggressive mass-deportation agenda, and immigration authorities have increasingly treated military families the same as any other undocumented case.

stories.title: India's Annapurni Subramaniam becomes the first Indian woman to win the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal
stories.what_happened: Subramaniam received the medal at the 46th COSPAR Scientific Assembly held this week in Florence, Italy, for her pioneering contributions to space research — particularly her work using India's AstroSat satellite (India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory) for ultraviolet astronomy, and her leadership role in the TMT collaboration, one of the world's largest astronomy projects. She becomes the first Indian woman and only the third woman worldwide to win the medal since it was instituted 36 years ago.
key_points: Prof. **Annapurni Subramaniam**, director of the **Indian Institute of Astrophysics**, wins the **2026 medal**
First Indian woman — and only the **third woman globally** — to receive the honor
Recognized for work on **AstroSat** and ultraviolet astronomy, plus the **Thirty Metre Telescope** project
Awarded at the **46th COSPAR Scientific Assembly** in Florence, Italy

depth.background: The **Vikram Sarabhai Medal** was created in 1990 to honor Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the physicist who founded India's space program and ISRO. It's jointly awarded every two years by the international **Committee on Space Research (COSPAR)** and ISRO to scientists from developing countries for outstanding contributions to space research. Past winners have mostly been men, making Subramaniam's win a notable milestone. She leads the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) in Bengaluru, one of India's premier astronomy research institutions, and has been central to India's role in the **Thirty Metre Telescope (TMT)**, a massive international observatory project.

stories.title: RBI holds its repo rate at 5.25% for a third straight meeting, betting inflation stays contained despite pricier oil
stories.what_happened: The RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee, meeting from August 3-5 under Governor **Sanjay Malhotra**, kept the benchmark **repo rate unchanged at 5.25%** — the third straight policy meeting without a change — and retained its **'neutral' policy stance**, meaning it isn't committing in advance to cut or hike next. The call was widely expected: in a Reuters survey of 72 economists, 68 predicted no change and only 4 expected a hike, with no one expecting a cut. Alongside the rate decision, the RBI projected India's **real GDP growth for FY27 (the year ending March 2027) at 6.6%** and **consumer price inflation (CPI) at 5.1%** for the year. Malhotra presented the decision at 10am IST, with a press conference to explain the committee's reasoning following at noon.
key_points: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee kept the **repo rate unchanged at 5.25%** for a **third consecutive meeting**.
The decision matched what **68 of 72 economists** in a Reuters poll had predicted — only 4 expected a hike.
The RBI projects **FY27 GDP growth of 6.6%** and **CPI inflation of 5.1%** for the year.
Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** announced the call at 10am, with a press conference to follow at noon.
The bank is **balancing above-target inflation** against **slowing growth** and **Middle East oil-price risk**.

depth.background: The **repo rate** is the interest rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks — it's the main lever the central bank uses to make borrowing cheaper or more expensive across the whole economy. India's central bank has held this rate steady for two meetings running as it tries to balance a delicate mix: inflation has crept slightly above the RBI's comfort zone, economic growth has been cooling, and global oil prices have been volatile because of the ongoing Middle East conflict, all of which cuts against a straightforward rate-cut or rate-hike call.

thread.previously: Economists expected the RBI to hold rates steady at its August 5 meeting, weighing Middle East-driven oil risk against a rupee that had been stabilizing.
thread.changed: The RBI has now actually made the call: repo rate held at 5.25% for a third straight meeting, with fresh FY27 growth (6.6%) and inflation (5.1%) projections attached.

stories.title: Alpine's F1 team valued at $3.5 billion as Christian Horner bids for Otro Capital's stake
stories.what_happened: Briatore says a new bid for Otro Capital's 24% Alpine stake values the whole team at roughly $3.5 billion — nearly four times its 2023 valuation. Horner has formally lodged a bid for that stake, positioning himself for a return to the sport in an ownership role rather than as a team principal. Company filings show Otro Capital cannot freely transfer its stake until September 2026, and Renault retains approval rights over any transaction before then, meaning the deal cannot close immediately even if terms are agreed.
key_points: Flavio Briatore claims a new offer values Alpine at **$3.5 billion**, up from **$900 million** in 2023
Former Red Bull boss **Christian Horner** has lodged a bid for Otro Capital's **24% stake**
Otro Capital — backed by **Ryan Reynolds, Travis Kelce and Rory McIlroy** — bought in for **$200 million** in 2023
Renault keeps **approval rights** over any sale until **September 2026**

depth.background: Renault Group sold a 24% stake in its Alpine Formula 1 team to investment group Otro Capital in 2023 for $200 million, valuing the team at $900 million at the time. Otro is now looking to exit that investment. Christian Horner, who spent two decades running Red Bull's championship-winning F1 team before departing the outfit, is now a free agent looking for his next role in the sport. Alpine executive advisor Flavio Briatore has repeatedly argued that F1 team valuations are exploding as the sport's global TV and streaming audience grows.

stories.title: Alonso's Aston Martin future now hinges on one thing: whether Honda's new engine actually works at Zandvoort
stories.what_happened: Alonso has confirmed he still hasn't made a decision on his 2027 future and expects to decide **around the Zandvoort and Monza races**, just after the summer break — consistent with what he'd said before. What's new is the specificity around what he's actually watching for: Aston Martin's new **Honda power unit**, which was tested after the Hungarian Grand Prix, is set to be paired with an upgraded **B-spec car** — the same car that reportedly impressed at the Hungaroring — for the post-break races. According to F1 journalist Joe Saward, Alonso is seriously considering a **move to Alpine** if that Honda-powered package doesn't show clear, convincing progress by Zandvoort. Alonso himself has said he wants to win a championship with Aston Martin, **"with or without driving,"** suggesting he sees his own future as tied to the team's trajectory either as a driver or in some other role.
key_points: Alonso says he'll likely decide his F1 future around **Zandvoort and Monza**, right after the summer break.
The trigger point: whether Aston Martin's new **Honda engine**, paired with an upgraded car, actually delivers pace.
Journalist Joe Saward reports Alonso is **eyeing a switch to Alpine** if Aston Martin doesn't show clear progress.
The new Honda power unit was tested after the Hungarian Grand Prix and pairs with a **B-spec car** that impressed at the Hungaroring.
Alonso, one of F1's biggest names without a 2027 contract, has said he still wants to **win a title with Aston Martin** — with or without driving it himself eventually.

depth.background: Aston Martin has struggled to match its ambitions since Alonso joined in 2023, and the team is banking heavily on a switch to **Honda engines** starting in 2026 to finally close the gap to the front-runners — a technical partnership seen as central to its long-term title hopes. Alonso, now in his 40s and one of the most respected drivers on the grid, has been managing his own timeline for retirement versus continuing, tying his decision explicitly to whether he believes the team's technical direction can produce a winning car before he's ready to step back.

thread.previously: Alonso said he hadn't made a decision yet on his F1 future and would likely wait until around the summer break to choose between staying at Aston Martin or retiring.
thread.changed: New reporting narrows down exactly what he's waiting to see: whether Aston Martin's new Honda engine, paired with an upgraded car, shows real pace at the Dutch Grand Prix — and adds that Alpine, not retirement, may be his real alternative if it doesn't.

stories.title: Audi's rocky-looking F1 debut is actually going better than the points table suggests, says racing director
stories.what_happened: Audi racing director **Allan McNish** said that, despite a modest points total so far, the team's actual car performance has been **better than expected**, particularly in qualifying trim. The team has scored 12 points total in its debut season, with 10 of those points coming across just the last three races, following upgrades introduced at the **Austrian Grand Prix** that targeted low-speed corner performance — upgrades that also helped driver Nico Hulkenberg score points in Hungary. McNish and other analysts argue the raw points tally doesn't reflect the car's true pace, pointing instead to a recurring issue getting the car off the line cleanly at race starts, which has cost the team results its underlying pace should have delivered.
key_points: Audi has scored **12 points** in its debut F1 season, with 10 of them coming in just the last three races
Racing director **Allan McNish** says the car is 'better in qualifying than I expected'
Upgrades introduced for the **Austrian Grand Prix**, focused on low-speed corners, are behind the recent uptick
Analysts rate Audi's chassis as possibly the **best outside the top four teams** in the midfield
The team, which took over the former **Sauber** squad, says slow starts off the grid have masked its true pace

depth.background: Audi entered Formula 1 as a full works team for 2026 by taking over the historic **Sauber** squad, one of several manufacturers joining the grid this season alongside Cadillac. Big-name manufacturer entries into F1 usually face a tough transition, since building a competitive car from scratch takes years even with a factory team's resources — so Audi's early-season points total looked like a rocky start by that standard.

stories.title: Racing Bulls deny reports Liam Lawson will be dropped for junior driver Nikola Tsolov
stories.what_happened: Spanish media reported this week that Red Bull junior driver **Nikola Tsolov** will replace **Liam Lawson** at Racing Bulls for 2027, reviving a running storyline about Lawson's future. Racing Bulls officials pushed back publicly, saying no decision has been made for next season. Separately, Racing Bulls boss **Alan Permane** has acknowledged that Tsolov is **'next in line'** for a seat in Red Bull's pipeline — a comment that, without confirming any swap, keeps pressure on Lawson. Tsolov himself issued a fresh public comment today on his own F1 prospects as the speculation continued. Lawson, demoted from the main Red Bull team after just two races in 2025, has rebuilt his reputation this year and sits **9th in the drivers' standings with 43 points** from 11 rounds, on a contract that runs only through the end of 2026.
key_points: **Spanish media reports** claim junior driver **Nikola Tsolov** will replace **Liam Lawson** at Racing Bulls for 2027.
**Racing Bulls officials have publicly denied** that any decision on the seat has been made.
Team boss **Alan Permane** has called Tsolov **'next in line'** in Red Bull's pipeline — without confirming a swap.
Lawson sits **9th in the standings with 43 points**, his best sustained F1 form, on a deal that **expires at the end of 2026**.
Lawson was **demoted from the main Red Bull team after just two races in 2025**, adding to his uncertain long-term standing.

depth.background: Liam Lawson is a Red Bull-backed driver promoted to the main Red Bull team for 2025 but demoted back to the junior team, Racing Bulls, after only two races — a bruising setback that put his long-term future with the Red Bull organization in doubt. Nikola Tsolov is a rising junior driver in Red Bull's development program, tipped as a future Racing Bulls candidate. Red Bull's junior program has a long history of favoring short-term contracts and swapping drivers on current form rather than committing long-term, which keeps pressure on incumbents like Lawson even when they perform well.

thread.previously: Yesterday, Lawson said he expected talks about his 2027 future to happen during F1's summer break, sitting 9th in the standings with 43 points on a contract that expires at the end of 2026, with Red Bull's junior programme known for favoring short-term deals.
thread.changed: Today, Spanish media reports claimed Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov will replace Lawson for 2027; Racing Bulls officials publicly denied any decision has been made, even as team boss Alan Permane separately called Tsolov 'next in line' in the pipeline — and Tsolov himself issued a fresh comment on his own prospects.

stories.title: The US is quietly negotiating to let Ukraine build its own Patriot missiles — even as Trump publicly balks
stories.what_happened: According to four sources cited by US News, the United States is continuing negotiations that would allow Ukraine to build its own Patriot interceptor missiles, potentially with Ukraine manufacturing some components domestically while final assembly happens elsewhere in Europe. The talks proceed even though President Trump told reporters the US has **'not agreed to'** letting Ukraine build the missiles, saying the US must be 'very careful about letting somebody build them' because advanced military technology 'is a hard thing to give away' — and a country that receives it 'could someday turn on you.' Ukraine has pushed hard for the deal because it needs a steady, secure domestic supply of PAC-3 interceptors to keep pace with Russia's intensifying missile and drone campaign. US officials are reportedly continuing to explore co-manufacturing arrangements despite the president's public hesitation.
key_points: The US is in active talks to let Ukraine **co-produce Patriot interceptor missiles**, including PAC-3s, despite Trump saying the US has **'not agreed'** to it.
Trump warned giving Ukraine missile-building technology is risky because a country that receives it 'could someday turn on you.'
One option under discussion: Ukraine builds **some components domestically**, with final assembly done elsewhere in Europe.
Ukraine wants the deal because PAC-3 interceptors are among the **few weapons that can shoot down** the ballistic missiles Russia is increasingly firing at Ukrainian cities.
Talks are continuing 'despite Trump's doubts,' according to **four sources** familiar with the discussions, per US News.

depth.background: Patriot is a US-made air-defense system that can shoot down incoming missiles and aircraft; its newest interceptor, the **PAC-3**, is one of the only weapons capable of intercepting the ballistic missiles Russia has increasingly used against Ukrainian cities. Since Russia's 2022 invasion, Ukraine has relied on donated and purchased Patriot batteries from the US and European allies, but supply has struggled to keep pace with Russia's growing missile and drone barrages. Letting Ukraine manufacture the missiles itself, instead of just receiving them, would be a major shift — advanced US missile technology has historically stayed tightly controlled and rarely shared even with close allies.

stories.title: A sacred Himalayan lake becomes India's 101st Ramsar wetland — and Arunachal Pradesh's first
stories.what_happened: The Indian government designated Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh's Kamlang Tiger Reserve as the country's **101st Ramsar site**, and the state's first ever. The lake spans **129 hectares** at an elevation of **1,168 metres** in the Eastern Himalayas, surrounded by dense forest recognized as a biodiversity hotspot, with more than **150 tree species** and **49 orchid species** recorded in the area. It provides habitat and a wintering ground for multiple waterbird species, plus over 20 species of reptiles and amphibians. The site is deeply significant to the **Mishmi tribe**, who consider it sacred under an animist belief system that reveres forests, wildlife and natural elements. The announcement came alongside a nationwide wetland-conservation campaign the Centre is running.
key_points: **Glaw Lake**, a freshwater lake inside the **Kamlang Tiger Reserve**, is now India's **101st Ramsar site** — a globally recognized 'wetland of international importance.'
It's **Arunachal Pradesh's first-ever** Ramsar site, sitting at **1,168 metres** in the Eastern Himalayas.
The **129-hectare** lake hosts over **150 tree species** and **49 orchid species**, and is a wintering ground for waterbirds and 20+ reptile/amphibian species.
India's Ramsar count has jumped from just **26 sites in 2014** to **101 today**.
The lake is **sacred to the Mishmi tribe**, whose animist, place-based traditions have helped conserve it for generations.

depth.background: The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty, signed in the Iranian city of Ramsar in 1971, under which countries designate globally significant wetlands — lakes, marshes, mangroves — and commit to conserving them. India has rapidly expanded its Ramsar list over the past decade as part of a broader wetland-conservation push, going from **26 designated sites in 2014 to 101 now**. Glaw Lake sits inside the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary in Arunachal Pradesh, India's remote, biodiverse northeast, and has long been considered sacred by the local Mishmi tribe, whose animist beliefs treat forests and natural features as spiritually significant — a belief system that protected the lake for generations before any government label existed.

stories.title: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, edging out establishment favorite Haley Stevens
stories.what_happened: Voters cast ballots Tuesday, and the Associated Press called the Democratic Senate primary for El-Sayed at **9:56 a.m. Wednesday**, once his roughly one-point lead over Stevens held with nearly all votes counted. El-Sayed overcame about **$65 million in outside spending** arrayed against him, including more than **$30 million from an AIPAC-aligned group** running ads for Stevens. Stevens had backing from much of the party's centrist establishment, who argued she was the safer bet to hold the seat. El-Sayed now advances to face former Republican Congressman **Mike Rogers** in the November 3 general election, a contest both parties see as pivotal to Senate control. The tight final margin meant the race couldn't be called until the morning after voting.
key_points: El-Sayed beat Rep. Haley Stevens by just **1 percentage point** once nearly all ballots were counted
The Associated Press called the race **Wednesday morning**, about a day after polls closed
A pro-Israel group aligned with **AIPAC spent over $30 million** backing Stevens — and still lost
El-Sayed advances to face Republican **Mike Rogers** in the November 3 general election
The result is being read as a win for the Democratic Party's **progressive wing** in a genuine swing state

depth.background: Michigan's Senate seat opened up because Sen. Gary Peters chose not to seek re-election, setting off a crowded, incumbent-free primary that yesterday's brief covered as voting got underway. Abdul El-Sayed is an epidemiologist and former Detroit health director who ran for Michigan governor in 2018 as a progressive insurgent, campaigning on **Medicare for All** and rejecting corporate PAC money. Haley Stevens is a sitting U.S. Representative who ran as the establishment-backed centrist and drew heavy outside spending, including from a pro-Israel super PAC. Michigan is one of a small number of true swing states whose Senate race could **tip control of the chamber** in 2027.

thread.previously: Michigan voters were casting primary ballots for governor, U.S. Senate, and all 13 U.S. House seats in open, incumbent-free races, with Rep. Haley Stevens and epidemiologist Abdul El-Sayed among the notable Democratic Senate candidates.
thread.changed: El-Sayed has now won the Democratic Senate primary over Stevens by about one point, overcoming $65 million in outside spending, and will face Republican Mike Rogers in November.

stories.title: Sensex jumps over 600 points and Nifty tops 24,650 as crude oil crashes below $80 on Hormuz deal hopes
stories.what_happened: Indian equity benchmarks opened sharply higher on **August 5**: the Sensex climbed **626.43 points (0.79%)** to open at **79,055.38**, and the Nifty added **54.3 points** to open at **24,669.20**, before pushing further to top **24,650** through the session. The rally tracked a global risk-on move as **Brent crude fell below $80 a barrel** amid growing hope that a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is close, easing the oil-supply fears that have weighed on markets for weeks. Aviation and logistics-linked stocks led gainers — **IndiGo rose 2.25%**, alongside Bharti Airtel, L&T, M&M, and UltraTech Cement — while **Titan, TCS, HDFC Bank, Sun Pharma, and BEL** lagged. Market breadth was strongly positive, with **1,827 advancing stocks to 458 declining** on the NSE in early trade, reflecting broad-based buying rather than a narrow rally. The move came the same day the **RBI held its repo rate steady at 5.25%** for a third consecutive policy meeting, a decision markets had been watching closely.
key_points: **Sensex opened up 626 points (0.79%)** to 79,055 and the Nifty added **54 points** to 24,669, before extending gains through the morning.
The rally rode global optimism as **Brent crude fell below $80 a barrel**, easing fears of an oil-price shock for India, the world's third-largest crude importer.
Gainers included **IndiGo (+2.25%), Bharti Airtel, L&T, M&M and UltraTech Cement**; laggards included **Titan, TCS, HDFC Bank, Sun Pharma and BEL**.
Market breadth was strongly positive, with **1,827 stocks advancing versus 458 declining** on the NSE in early trade.
The rally came the same day the **RBI held its repo rate steady at 5.25%** for a third straight meeting.

depth.background: India imports roughly **85% of its crude oil**, so global oil-price swings hit the economy fast — through the rupee, inflation, and airline and logistics costs — more than almost any other major economy. Since late July, fears of a wider Iran-Israel-US conflict spilling into the **Strait of Hormuz** had kept oil prices elevated and Indian markets on edge, with a four-day rally snapping into a decline just yesterday. When that geopolitical risk eased — after Trump held off on strikes in favor of a possible Hormuz-reopening deal — oil prices fell sharply, and Indian markets, like global peers, rallied on the relief.

stories.title: Manipal Health's ₹9,275 crore IPO lists with an 11% pop, India's second-largest IPO this year
stories.what_happened: Manipal Health Enterprises made its stock-market debut on Wednesday, with shares listing at **₹655** on the BSE — an **11% premium** over its ₹590 issue price — and settling around ₹652 on the NSE, a similar gain. The **₹9,275 crore** initial public offering comprised an ₹8,000 crore fresh issue of new shares and a ₹1,275 crore offer-for-sale by existing shareholders. At its listing price, the hospital chain commands a market capitalization of roughly **₹859 billion (about $10 billion)**, making it India's third-largest listed hospital operator behind Apollo Hospitals Enterprise and Max Healthcare Institute. The debut beat expectations implied by grey-market trading ahead of the listing, and the $960 million raise ranks as India's second-largest IPO this year.
key_points: **Manipal Health Enterprises** shares listed at **₹655** on the BSE, an **11% premium** over the ₹590 issue price.
The **₹9,275 crore (~$960 million) IPO** is India's **second-largest** so far this year.
At the listing price, Manipal Health is valued at roughly **₹859 billion (~$10 billion)**.
It's now India's **third-largest listed hospital operator**, behind **Apollo Hospitals** and **Max Healthcare**.
The issue combined a **₹8,000 crore fresh issue** with a **₹1,275 crore offer-for-sale**.

depth.background: Manipal Health Enterprises runs one of India's largest private hospital chains, competing with Apollo Hospitals and Max Healthcare in a sector that has drawn heavy investor interest as India's rising middle class spends more on private healthcare and health-insurance penetration grows. The IPO opened for subscription on July 29 and closed July 31, 2026. Big hospital-chain IPOs have become a recurring theme in India's markets this year as private-equity investors look to cash out of healthcare bets built up over the past decade.

stories.title: LIC's ₹3,300 crore retail share sale opens today at a discount, a day after institutions oversubscribed it 3.3x
stories.what_happened: The government's LIC stake sale — a base **2.5% stake with an option to sell up to 4% more** — opened for institutional investors on **August 4** at a floor price of **₹382 per share** and was **oversubscribed 3.3 times**, prompting the government to expand the offer size to capture the extra demand and raise roughly **$3.3 billion**. Despite the strong institutional appetite, **LIC's stock fell 7.86% on Tuesday to ₹391**, reflecting the market pricing in dilution from the new supply hitting the market. The offer opens for **retail investors today, August 5**, giving ordinary investors a chance to buy at the same discounted floor price. This sale is one step toward a regulatory deadline requiring LIC to lift its public float to **10% by May 2027** and **25%** over the longer term.
key_points: The government is selling up to **6.5% of its stake in LIC**, worth up to **$3.3 billion (~₹31,400 crore)**, through an Offer for Sale (OFS).
Retail investors can buy in **today, August 5**, a day after institutions oversubscribed their portion **3.3 times**.
The floor price is **₹382 a share — a 10% discount** to Monday's closing price.
LIC stock still fell nearly **8% on Tuesday** even with strong institutional demand, as the market absorbed the extra supply.
The sale is part of a **SEBI-mandated push** to lift LIC's public shareholding to 10% by May 2027, and 25% eventually.

depth.background: **LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India)** is India's largest insurer and, since its 2022 IPO, has remained majority-owned by the government — but stock-market rules require every listed company to eventually have at least 25% of its shares freely traded by the public, and LIC is still far below that. To close the gap, the government periodically sells down its stake through an **Offer for Sale**, where big investors and later retail investors buy shares directly from the government rather than the company issuing new ones. Because these sales pump a large new supply of shares onto the market at once, they usually come at a **discount to the prevailing price** to make sure buyers show up, which tends to pull the stock price down even as the government successfully raises cash.

thread.previously: We reported the government's ₹31,400 crore LIC share sale was oversubscribed 3.3 times by institutional investors on August 4, even as the stock tumbled 8.7% that day.
thread.changed: The sale now opens for retail investors today, August 5, at the same discounted floor price, after the government expanded the offer size to capture the extra institutional demand.

stories.title: IPL 2027: Rishabh Pant returns to Delhi Capitals as Kuldeep Yadav moves to Lucknow in a blockbuster trade
stories.what_happened: Delhi Capitals and Lucknow Super Giants completed a direct player swap: Pant returns to Delhi — the franchise that developed him — at a lower salary of ₹15 crore, while left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav moves to Lucknow on his existing ₹13.5 crore contract. The trade comes amid a broader wave of early trade activity ahead of the November 2026 mini-auction, with separate speculation swirling that Hardik Pandya could leave Mumbai Indians, with Kolkata Knight Riders and Rajasthan Royals both reportedly interested.
key_points: **Rishabh Pant** rejoins **Delhi Capitals** on a revised **₹15 crore** salary, down from the **₹27 crore** LSG paid for him in 2025
**Kuldeep Yadav** leaves Delhi after **five seasons** to join **Lucknow Super Giants** on his existing **₹13.5 crore** deal
Comes as the **IPL 2027 trade window**, open since late June, heats up ahead of the **November mini-auction**
**Hardik Pandya's** possible exit from Mumbai Indians is also being speculated, with KKR and Rajasthan Royals interested

depth.background: The IPL lets franchises trade contracted players (with or without cash) outside the formal once-a-year auction, via a trade window that reopens each off-season. Pant became the most expensive player in IPL history when Lucknow Super Giants bought him for ₹27 crore at the 2025 mega-auction; Kuldeep had been with Delhi Capitals for five seasons. Both are current India internationals, making this trade one of the biggest player swaps in IPL history.

stories.title: Lawson and rookie Lindblad are quietly racing each other for F1's most coveted empty seat: Red Bull's
stories.what_happened: Racing Bulls drivers Liam Lawson and rookie Arvid Lindblad have had contrasting starts to the 2026 season — Lindblad scored points on debut at the season-opening Australian Grand Prix, while Lawson had a difficult start after nearly being hit by Franco Colapinto off the grid. Since then, Lawson has pulled ahead in the championship, sitting on **43 points** to Lindblad's **23**. Former IndyCar driver James Hinchcliffe has publicly predicted Racing Bulls could claim a podium finish this season, with commentators suggesting either driver could capitalize in a mixed-up, rain-affected race. Analysts increasingly frame the pair's on-track form this season as a real audition for a future seat at parent team Red Bull, though a seat opening there is far from guaranteed.
key_points: Racing Bulls teammates **Liam Lawson** and rookie **Arvid Lindblad** are both out of contract at the end of 2026.
Lawson currently leads their internal battle with **43 points** to Lindblad's 23 in the drivers' standings.
Lindblad scored points on his very first race, the **Australian Grand Prix**, as a rookie.
Pundits increasingly frame the pair as future rivals for a seat at parent team **Red Bull**, though a vacancy is far from guaranteed.

depth.background: Racing Bulls (formerly AlphaTauri, and before that Toro Rosso) is Red Bull's junior F1 team, historically used to develop young drivers before promoting the best of them to the main Red Bull team — Max Verstappen himself came through this pipeline. For 2026, Red Bull placed **rookie Arvid Lindblad** alongside experienced driver **Liam Lawson**, who was demoted back to Racing Bulls after a rocky spell driving for Red Bull's senior team in 2025. Both drivers are out of contract at the end of this season, and with Red Bull's own senior lineup facing uncertainty, the junior team's driver pairing has become a proxy battle for F1 insiders trying to read Red Bull's succession plans.

stories.title: Aiden Markram quits The Hundred midway and flies home to South Africa for personal reasons; Jos Buttler takes over as Manchester captain
stories.what_happened: Manchester Super Giants confirmed that captain Aiden Markram is leaving The Hundred 2026 immediately and returning to South Africa for personal reasons, missing the rest of the tournament. Markram had played five matches for Manchester this season, scoring 117 runs, before his departure at a crucial stage of the competition. The franchise has handed the captaincy to **Jos Buttler**, who has been in outstanding form with **226 runs in five matches at an average of 112**, marking his first time leading a franchise side since England's 2025 Champions Trophy campaign. New Zealand all-rounder **Michael Bracewell** has been signed as a straight replacement for Markram in the squad.
key_points: Markram leaves Manchester Super Giants after **5 matches and 117 runs** this season
**Jos Buttler**, in career-best form with **226 runs at an average of 112**, becomes the new captain
New Zealand all-rounder **Michael Bracewell** signs as Markram's like-for-like replacement
It's Buttler's first franchise captaincy since the **2025 Champions Trophy**

depth.background: The Hundred is an English short-format cricket competition, shorter than T20, played by eight city-based franchise teams over a few weeks each August. Aiden Markram, the South African batter, was named Manchester Super Giants' captain for the 2026 competition and had been in decent form before his sudden departure. Jos Buttler is a former England white-ball captain and one of the most experienced leaders in franchise cricket globally, giving Manchester an experienced deputy to step straight into the role.

stories.title: Carlos Sainz confirms Williams contract talks as he admits he's unsure about his F1 future
stories.what_happened: Carlos Sainz confirmed he has plans to sit down with Williams team principal **James Vowles** to discuss his future with the team, but said he remains unsure when a decision will actually be reached, adding that he will weigh his options during the F1 summer break. His current Williams contract expires at the **end of 2026**. Reports indicate Williams has responded with a substantial contract offer — described by some outlets as a 'world champion's' offer — to try to retain him, as the team looks to hold onto experienced talent after slipping from a surprise podium-scoring team in 2025 to more of a backmarker through much of the 2026 season.
key_points: Sainz's current Williams contract runs out at the **end of this season**
He confirmed he will sit down with team boss **James Vowles** to discuss his future
Reports say Williams has made a **'world champion's' offer** to try to keep him
Sainz says a decision will be made during the **summer break**
Williams has fallen from surprise podium-scorer last year to a **backmarker** for much of 2026

depth.background: Carlos Sainz joined Williams for the 2025 season after leaving Ferrari, and the team showed encouraging progress last year, including a couple of surprise podium finishes. The F1 'driver market' for 2027 has been unusually active this summer, with several high-profile seats — including at Alpine, Aston Martin, and Red Bull — still unresolved, giving experienced drivers like Sainz leverage to weigh multiple options.

stories.title: Ukraine says a North Korean missile unit — 120 ballistic missiles — is deploying inside Russia
stories.what_happened: Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR), through spokesperson **Andrii Cherniak**, said Russia is deploying a North Korean missile unit — roughly **90 servicemen** from North Korea's 112th Missile Brigade — to Russia's **Voronezh region**, near the Ukrainian border. The unit is expected to be equipped with **six launchers and 120 KN-23/KN-24 ballistic missiles**, though exact numbers are still being finalized at high-level talks planned for next month. This would mark a significant expansion of North Korea's role, from supplying weapons to potentially operating missile systems directly against Ukraine. Pyongyang has already sent a fresh shipment of **40 KN-23/KN-24 missiles** along with personnel. The claim follows Russia's late-July missile strike on Ukraine, the first confirmed use of North Korean ballistic missiles since **August 2025**.
key_points: Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) says Russia is deploying a **North Korean missile unit** of about **90 servicemen** to Russia's Voronezh region.
The unit is expected to field **six launchers and 120 KN-23/KN-24 ballistic missiles**.
It would be the first time North Korean troops directly **operate missile systems on Russian soil**, not just supply weapons.
Pyongyang has already shipped **40 KN-23/KN-24 missiles** and personnel; final numbers are set at **high-level talks next month**.
Russia's **late-July strike** on Ukraine used North Korean missiles for the first time since **August 2025**.

depth.background: Since late 2023, Russia has fired dozens of North Korean-made ballistic missiles at Ukraine as part of a deepening military partnership between Moscow and Pyongyang, which has also included North Korea sending troops to fight in Russia's Kursk region. That cooperation has expanded as Russia's war effort grinds on, with Pyongyang trading weapons and manpower for money, food, and technology transfers. Ukrainian intelligence tracks these transfers closely and issues periodic public warnings meant to both alert allies and pressure Moscow and Pyongyang diplomatically.

stories.title: Iran and Oman say they've reached a Hormuz shipping-route deal, with a US announcement possible this week
stories.what_happened: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman **Esmail Baghaei** said Wednesday that Tehran and Muscat have reached an agreement on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint statement now in its 'final drafting' stage. Under the emerging arrangement, commercial ships would enter the Persian Gulf through a route controlled by **Iran** and exit through a separate route controlled by **Oman**, with fees charged for security and environmental protection along the way. President Trump said the wider, US-brokered deal to fully reopen the strait 'could come as early as Wednesday,' a day after his Treasury Secretary said an agreement was possible 'within days.' Baghaei described the Oman talks as 'professional' and 'forward-moving,' but repeated that Iran is not negotiating directly with the United States — even as US officials describe the negotiations as active. The announcement comes just two days after Trump warned Iran it had a **'last chance'** to sign a deal before facing renewed strikes aimed at its leadership.
key_points: Iran's foreign ministry says a **shipping-route agreement** with Oman has been reached, with a joint statement now in **final drafting**
Under the emerging plan, ships would enter the Gulf via an **Iranian-controlled route** and exit via an **Oman-controlled route**, with security fees charged
Trump says the wider deal could be announced '**today or tomorrow**' — just a day after threatening to resume strikes on Iran's leadership
This is Iran's **second straight day** of denying it is negotiating directly with Washington, even as the US insists talks are active
Oil prices have already fallen on hopes the world's most important oil chokepoint fully reopens

depth.background: The Strait of Hormuz is the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which roughly **a fifth of the world's oil** passes, and it has been the center of a months-long crisis since strikes disrupted shipping there and Iran's Supreme Leader was killed in a February strike that triggered open war. The US and Iran agreed to a ceasefire earlier this year, but the strait has stayed a flashpoint — a Greek-owned tanker was hit by an unknown projectile only yesterday. Trump has oscillated between threatening renewed 'leadership-targeting' strikes and touting an imminent reopening deal, while Tehran has consistently denied talking directly to Washington, saying it negotiates only with Oman on how ships pass through.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported Trump had given Iran a 'last chance' to sign a Hormuz deal or face renewed strikes explicitly aimed at Iran's leadership, while Tehran kept denying it was negotiating directly with Washington.
thread.changed: Iran's foreign ministry now says it has reached an actual shipping-route agreement with Oman, with a joint statement in final drafting and Trump saying a full announcement could land within a day or two.

stories.title: Ajinkya Rahane retires from all cricket, closing a 17-year career that included India's historic 2020-21 Australia series win
stories.what_happened: Rahane announced his retirement from all forms of cricket via an emotional video message posted on social media, ending a career that spanned **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is** for India over 17 years. He said the time had come to move on, comparing timing in life to timing in batting. The defining moment of his career came as stand-in captain during India's 2020-21 tour of Australia: after India was bowled out for just **36 runs** in the first Test at Adelaide — its lowest-ever Test total — Rahane led the team to a stunning **2-1 series win**, widely regarded as one of Indian cricket's greatest achievements. His last India appearance came in a Test in the West Indies in July 2023. He continued playing domestic and franchise cricket afterward, most recently captaining Kolkata Knight Riders in IPL 2026, where he scored 335 runs in 14 matches.
key_points: Former India vice-captain **Ajinkya Rahane**, 38, has retired from **all formats of cricket** with immediate effect.
He played **85 Tests, 90 ODIs, and 20 T20Is** for India across a **17-year career**.
His career highlight: leading India to a **historic 2-1 Test series win in Australia (2020-21)** — after India was bowled out for **36 runs** in the first Test.
He last played competitively in **IPL 2026**, captaining Kolkata Knight Riders to **335 runs in 14 matches**.
His last India appearance was a **Test in the West Indies in July 2023**.

depth.background: Rahane made his India Test debut in 2013 and became one of the team's most reliable middle-order batters, known for his composure in tough overseas conditions. He briefly captained India in Virat Kohli's absence, most memorably during the 2020-21 tour of Australia. His international career effectively wound down after 2023, though he continued playing franchise cricket, most recently captaining Kolkata Knight Riders in IPL 2026.

stories.title: Adani Ports posts 9% profit growth as India's biggest port operator shrugs off global trade headwinds
stories.what_happened: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone reported **Q1 FY26 (April-June) net profit up roughly 9% year-on-year**, with revenue climbing about **19%** to over ₹9,100 crore. EBITDA — earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, a measure of core operating profit — rose in the double digits. The standout growth came from newer businesses: **logistics revenue nearly doubled** year-on-year to around ₹1,169 crore, and marine revenue nearly tripled to ₹541 crore. Domestic ports posted 12% revenue growth and 11% EBITDA growth even though cargo volumes grew only about 2%, meaning the company earned more per unit of cargo handled. Despite the beat on revenue and profit, the stock fell around 3% in trading, suggesting the market had expected even stronger numbers or was reacting to broader market moves.
key_points: Adani Ports' Q1 FY26 **net profit rose about 9% year-on-year** to roughly ₹3,600 crore
**Revenue jumped 19%** on the back of strong logistics and marine businesses
**EBITDA climbed 13-19%**, with logistics revenue nearly doubling year-on-year
Domestic ports grew revenue 12% even though cargo **volumes rose just 2%**, showing pricing power
Shares still **fell around 3%** after the results, as investors had priced in even stronger numbers

depth.background: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) is India's largest private port operator, run by the Adani Group, and handles a large share of the country's containerized and bulk cargo trade across more than a dozen ports. The company has been diversifying beyond pure port handling into logistics (moving goods inland from ports) and marine services, which tend to carry higher margins than basic cargo handling. Its results are watched as a bellwether for India's trade volumes, since ports are where imports and exports physically pass through.

stories.title: Haas is 'quietly disappearing' from F1's midfield as boss admits the team still isn't spending to the budget cap
stories.what_happened: Haas failed to score a single championship point across its final five races before the 2026 summer break, sliding to the back of the midfield pack. Speaking to media including PlanetF1, Komatsu confirmed Haas still isn't operating at the sport's **$215 million budget cap** ceiling, saying "we're not" there yet and calling it "one of the top priorities on my job list to be able to fund this team so that we can operate at the budget cap." He said the team's underperformance comes down to being financially "fighting with both hands tied" compared with rivals who can spend closer to the full allowance on upgrades. The result is that Haas, despite flashes of competitive pace earlier in the season, has been steadily out-developed as the year has gone on — a repeat of the pattern Komatsu was hired to fix.
key_points: Haas scored **zero points in its last five races** before the summer break
Team principal **Ayao Komatsu** admits Haas is not yet spending up to the **$215 million budget cap**
Komatsu calls funding the team to the cap **'one of the top priorities'** on his job list
Rivals with similar or smaller budgets have **out-developed** Haas's car through the season

depth.background: Formula 1 imposes a **$215 million budget cap** on how much each team can spend developing and running its cars each season, meant to level the field between giant manufacturer-backed teams and smaller independents. Haas is one of F1's smallest operations, without the in-house manufacturing depth of rivals like Ferrari or Mercedes, so how close it gets to that cap each year has always shaped how competitive its car can be. Team boss Ayao Komatsu took over in 2024 promising to fix Haas's historically weak in-season development, where it would start races well but fade as rivals upgraded their cars. Heading into the 2026 summer break, that old problem appears to have resurfaced.

stories.title: Russia's biggest missile-and-drone barrage in weeks kills 17 in Kyiv as Ukraine runs out of interceptors
stories.what_happened: Overnight into Wednesday, Russia launched one of its largest combined strikes of the war on Kyiv and the surrounding region: **24 ballistic missiles**, four hypersonic Zircon or supersonic Oniks missiles, and **115 drones**, many of them jet-powered. Ukraine's air force said preliminary data showed **none of the missiles were intercepted**, with impacts recorded across 26 locations. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said at least **17 people were killed and 44 wounded**, with rescue teams still searching rubble for survivors. He said the missiles mainly hit civilian infrastructure "with no connection to the war," including a brewing company, building-materials warehouses, a railway station, and apartment blocks, with one university building also damaged. Zelenskyy directly linked the deaths to Ukraine's shortage of Patriot interceptors, saying they "could have saved the lives of those killed today."
key_points: Russia fired **24 ballistic missiles**, 4 hypersonic/supersonic missiles, and **115 drones** at Kyiv overnight — one of the largest barrages of the war.
**17 people killed** and 44 wounded; Ukraine's air force says **none of the missiles were intercepted**.
Zelenskyy says strikes hit **civilian targets 'with no connection to the war'** — a brewery, building-materials warehouses, a railway station.
Ukraine is critically short of **Patriot interceptor missiles**, the only system that can stop incoming ballistic missiles.
Impacts were recorded across **26 locations** in and around the capital.

depth.background: Russia has repeatedly escalated long-range strikes on Ukrainian cities through the war, aiming to break morale and degrade infrastructure while ground fighting grinds on in the east. Ukraine's air defense leans heavily on US-supplied **Patriot systems** — the only ones able to shoot down Russia's ballistic missiles — but Western interceptor supplies haven't kept pace with the frequency of Russian barrages. The attack lands as Western diplomatic attention has been unusually focused on the Iran/Strait of Hormuz standoff, leaving Ukraine's war comparatively less in the spotlight even as it continues. Kyiv has faced repeated mass strikes this year, but officials describe this as among the largest in weeks.

stories.title: Russia's biggest strike in weeks kills 17 in Kyiv as Ukraine runs out of missile interceptors
stories.what_happened: Overnight into Wednesday, Russia launched one of its largest combined strikes on Kyiv in weeks: **115 drones and 28 missiles**, including **24 ballistic missiles** and four anti-ship missiles, aimed at the capital and the wider Kyiv region. Ukraine's air defenses shot down 98 of the drones, but confirmed **none of the 28 missiles were intercepted** — the first time in a while Kyiv's Patriot batteries came up completely empty against an attack of this scale. At least **17 people were killed and 44 wounded**, per Zelenskyy, with strikes and impacts recorded across 26 separate locations. Zelenskyy said the hit sites included ordinary civilian businesses — a brewery, a construction-materials warehouse, a mail depot — that had **no connection to the war**; Russia's defense ministry countered that it struck transport, logistics and drone-component distribution centers it says were tied to Ukraine's military effort. Regardless of who's right about the targets, the underlying fact both sides agree on is that Ukraine's ballistic-missile defenses simply weren't there Wednesday night.
key_points: Russia fired **115 drones and 28 missiles** at Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight — **not one missile was shot down**.
**17 people killed and 44 wounded**, President Zelenskyy said, in the deadliest single strike on the capital region in weeks.
Targets included a **brewery, a building-materials warehouse and a mail-sorting office** — sites Zelenskyy says had nothing to do with the war.
Ukraine's air force intercepted 98 of the drones but had **zero working interceptors left for incoming ballistic missiles**.
Russia's defense ministry disputes this, claiming it hit **military logistics and drone-component storage sites**.

depth.background: Russia has spent 2026 leaning harder on long-range missile and drone barrages as its ground offensive grinds on slowly, and Kyiv has depended almost entirely on US-made **Patriot air-defense batteries** to stop the ballistic missiles that regular anti-air guns can't reach. Those Patriot systems only work if they have interceptor missiles to fire, and Ukraine's stockpile has been shrinking for months faster than allies have resupplied it — partly because the same interceptors are in global demand after this year's Iran war. Zelenskyy has repeatedly and publicly asked the US and Europe for more, warning this exact scenario (a night with zero interceptions) was coming.

stories.title: HP, Asus and Acer start using Chinese memory chips in laptops as an AI-fueled shortage sends prices soaring
stories.what_happened: Three of the world's biggest PC makers — **HP, Asus, and Acer** — have started using small volumes of DRAM chips made by China's CXMT in some laptop models, according to a new report, marking the first time major Western PC brands have turned to Chinese memory chips at scale. The shift is a direct response to what industry insiders call an unprecedented memory shortage: AI data-center construction is expected to absorb **70% of all memory chip production in 2026**, a surge that has nearly **tripled DRAM prices over the past 18 months**. For now, the Chinese chips are being used only in a limited number of notebooks sold outside the US market, since CXMT is still prioritizing domestic customers like Huawei over export volume. CXMT itself posted **$7.5 billion in first-quarter 2026 revenue**, up **719% year-over-year**, and is preparing an **$8.6 billion IPO** as it becomes the world's fourth-largest memory-chip maker.
key_points: **HP, Asus, and Acer** have begun using Chinese-made DRAM chips from **CXMT** in some laptops sold outside the US.
AI data-center buildouts are set to consume **70% of global memory-chip production** in 2026.
DRAM prices have **nearly tripled in 18 months** as AI companies buy up memory supply.
CXMT, now the world's **fourth-largest memory maker**, is preparing an **$8.6 billion IPO**.
The Chinese chips are limited to non-US models for now, as CXMT still prioritizes domestic customers like Huawei.

depth.background: Dynamic random-access memory, or **DRAM**, is the fast, short-term memory every laptop, phone and server needs — and for years the market has been dominated by South Korea's Samsung and SK Hynix, and the US's Micron. As AI companies built out massive data centers over the past two years, they started buying nearly all the high-end memory those firms could make, squeezing out ordinary PC and phone makers. China has spent billions building its own memory-chip industry, led by state-backed **ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT)**, partly to reduce reliance on foreign chips amid US export controls.

stories.title: Cadillac's rookie F1 season earns a 'respectable' midseason grade despite zero points
stories.what_happened: At the season's summer break, Cadillac sits **11th and last** in the constructors' standings with **no points scored**, but midseason reviews from F1 media are crediting the team with a respectable start and a **'C' grade** for a rookie operation. The team's closest brush with scoring came at a penalty-heavy **Monaco Grand Prix**, where Perez finished **11th**, just outside the points. Through the season, incremental upgrades have let Cadillac **consistently outpace and jump ahead of Aston Martin** on pace, even as the team held back a larger update package for the **Hungarian Grand Prix**. Separately, Cadillac added **Pietro Fittipaldi**, a former F1 driver, as a development driver working in the simulator to help prepare the team for a fuller season ahead.
key_points: Cadillac, F1's newest team, sits **11th and last** in the standings with **zero points** at the summer break.
Veteran drivers **Sergio Perez** and **Valtteri Bottas** came close to scoring at a chaotic **Monaco Grand Prix**, finishing just outside the points.
Reviewers gave the team a **'C' grade** for a respectable rookie debut.
Upgrades through the season let Cadillac **consistently outpace Aston Martin**, even before a major update arrives at Hungary.
**Pietro Fittipaldi** joined as a development driver, working in the simulator ahead of the team's first full season.

depth.background: Cadillac became Formula 1's **11th team** and its newest entrant in 2026, backed by General Motors, joining the grid after a lengthy FIA approval process. Brand-new teams historically struggle in their debut seasons — building a competitive F1 car from scratch takes years, and rookie outfits often finish last while they learn. Cadillac hired two experienced grand prix winners, **Sergio Perez** and **Valtteri Bottas**, specifically to help develop the car and avoid rookie driving mistakes on top of an already difficult debut.

stories.title: Anthropic starts building its own AI chips to make Claude cheaper to run
stories.what_happened: On August 5, Anthropic confirmed it is building an internal chip-design team, led technically by Clive Chan, who joined Anthropic in June 2026 after previously working on OpenAI's chip team and, before that, Tesla's Dojo supercomputer program. The company is hiring semiconductor engineers — offering salaries between **$320,000 and $485,000** — who have taken chip designs from architecture through to actual production. The plan is to **co-design the chips and Claude's models together**, tailoring the hardware specifically to Claude's attention mechanisms (the part of the model that decides what information to focus on), targeting roughly a **50% cut in per-token inference costs**. Samsung has reportedly been explored as a manufacturing partner. Anthropic says it isn't abandoning its existing suppliers — Nvidia, AMD, AWS, and Google — the custom chips would simply add another layer to its infrastructure.
key_points: Anthropic is assembling an **in-house silicon team** to design custom chips tailored to Claude.
The goal: cut Claude's **per-token inference costs roughly in half** by co-designing hardware and software together.
It's hiring chip engineers with **production semiconductor experience**, paying up to **$485,000**.
**Samsung** has reportedly been explored as a manufacturing partner.
Anthropic says it will **keep buying** from Nvidia, AMD, AWS, and Google — the custom chips add a layer, not a replacement.

depth.background: Running a large AI model isn't just about training it once — every single reply it gives (called **inference**) costs computing power, and that ongoing cost is a huge and growing expense for AI companies as usage scales. Major AI labs increasingly design their own chips instead of relying only on off-the-shelf hardware: Google has its TPUs, Amazon has Trainium, and OpenAI has its own chip-design effort. Custom silicon lets a company tailor the chip's architecture to exactly how its own model works, which can meaningfully cut costs and reduce dependence on Nvidia, whose GPUs currently dominate — and are expensive and supply-constrained.

stories.title: Iran and Oman edge toward a Hormuz shipping deal, but Trump warns of new strikes if talks collapse
stories.what_happened: On Wednesday, Trump said negotiations with Iran would resume, while Tehran said its agreement with Oman on a new Hormuz shipping route was nearing completion — Iran called it the **'final stage'** of drafting. Trump said the eventual deal would include the **'immediate, complete and total'** reopening of the strait and address Iran's nuclear program, but stressed that immediate reopening wasn't guaranteed since navigation-control disputes remain unresolved: Washington wants free international navigation, Tehran wants a role in managing passage. Trump warned that if Iran backs out, he'll return to strikes. Iran's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, denies any direct US talks, saying it's negotiating only with Oman. The arrangement is reportedly contingent on the US lifting its blockade on Iranian ports.
key_points: Iran says it's in the **'final stage'** of drafting a shipping-route agreement with Oman over the **Strait of Hormuz**.
Trump says a deal covering the strait **and** Iran's nuclear program could be announced **this week**.
Trump warned: **'The Strait's going to be open very soon or they are going to get hit very hard.'**
Iran's Foreign Ministry denies **direct talks with Washington**, insisting it's negotiating only with Oman.
A previously planned **US strike** on Iran remains on hold while the talks continue.

depth.background: The **Strait of Hormuz** is a narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman that roughly **one-fifth of the world's oil** passes through — whoever controls access to it can squeeze global energy supply. Tensions have simmered for months between the US and Iran, including a period earlier this year when Washington threatened and then paused military strikes on Iranian targets. Trump has repeatedly claimed a Hormuz deal is close, only for talks to stall, while Tehran has consistently said it's negotiating shipping arrangements with neighboring **Oman**, not with the US directly.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported Iran and Oman said they'd reached a shipping-route deal for the Strait of Hormuz, with a US announcement possible this week.
thread.changed: Trump now says there's been no breakthrough yet — Iran insists it's negotiating only with Oman, not the US directly — and Trump is threatening renewed strikes if the deal collapses, even as Iran calls the Oman agreement's drafting the 'final stage'.

stories.title: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff threatens to bench a driver if the Antonelli-Russell title fight turns toxic
stories.what_happened: Wolff revealed that Mercedes has been strategically timing which upgrades go on which car, holding back a chunk of planned upgrades for the second half of 2026 specifically to manage the championship fight between Antonelli and Russell. Antonelli currently leads the drivers' standings with 219 points, 50 clear of Ferrari's Hamilton in second and 59 ahead of Russell, who has struggled with what he describes as power-unit reliability issues. Wolff stated plainly that if the two teammates' rivalry escalates beyond what he considers reasonable — echoing the team's bruising Hamilton-Rosberg years — he is willing to bench or drop one of them to protect the team.
key_points: Mercedes rookie **Kimi Antonelli** leads the drivers' standings on **219 points**.
Antonelli is **50 points clear** of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in 2nd, and **59 points** ahead of his own teammate **George Russell**.
Team boss **Toto Wolff** says Mercedes has deliberately **held back upgrades** for the second half of the season to manage the title fight.
Wolff has explicitly warned he's prepared to **bench or drop a driver** if the Antonelli-Russell rivalry crosses reasonable limits.
Russell says his slump is partly down to **power-unit issues**, not just being outpaced by his 18-year-old teammate.

Team principal Toto Wolff has publicly referenced Mercedes' painful Hamilton-Rosberg rivalry from the mid-2010s, which turned bitter and cost the team on-track incidents, as the reason he wants to manage this year's intra-team dynamic more carefully.

thread.previously: On August 3 we reported Antonelli held a commanding 50-point championship lead heading into the summer break.
thread.changed: Today, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff revealed the team has deliberately held back upgrades to manage the title fight, and explicitly threatened to bench either Antonelli or Russell if their rivalry turns toxic — echoing the team's bitter Hamilton-Rosberg era.
